subject.title: [Feature]: Fallback approval mode + model attribution in messages

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in approval gate before executing configured model fallbacks, and if so should it be per-agent, per-session, or routed through an existing approval/channel event contract?
rationale: The remaining request would change fallback runtime behavior and add operator-facing config; repository policy treats fallback behavior and config surface as compatibility- and product-sensitive.

options.title: Design a core opt-in fallback gate
options.body: Define a default-off approval contract with timeout behavior, channel delivery semantics, and upgrade-safe config before implementation.

options.title: Keep fallback automatic
options.body: Treat current fallback notices plus response-prefix attribution as the supported visibility/control model and close this direction as not planned.

options.title: Route through plugin/API design first
options.body: Define an extension hook for approval decisions instead of adding a one-off core model config key.

recommendation.title: Design a core opt-in fallback gate
recommendation.body: Define a default-off approval contract with timeout behavior, channel delivery semantics, and upgrade-safe config before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current-history route for fallback notices, model-failover docs, and the config-sensitive product decision.
